evidence.before: async function listItems(transport) { const body = await request(transport, '/items'); return body.items; }
evidence.caption: Before, listItems made one request and returned only body.items. After, npm test covers multi-page order/cursor forwarding and null or absent cursor termination (5/5 passing).

pr.body: Implemented cursor iteration in client.js using the existing transport request convention: the first request has an empty query, and subsequent requests pass the returned cursor without modification. Added tests for ordered multi-page results, exact opaque cursor forwarding, and terminal null or absent cursors. Updated README.md. Verified with `npm test` (5/5 passed) and `git diff --check` (passed). Assumption: API responses follow the shared contract and provide an items array.
pr.summary: Made listItems return the full ordered inventory across API pages. Before: it read only the first response; now: it follows each next_cursor until null or absent.
pr.title: Follow cursor pages when listing items

risk.why: Contained behavior change behind existing listItems interface, touching client.js, tests, and README. It adds pagination requests but has no security, persistence, or concurrency impact. The full test suite passes; all three reviewers found no issues.

item.title: Implement cursor pagination for GET /items
item.brief: Implement GET /items cursor pagination per the shared contract. Preserve ordering by id. Validate limit as an integer from 1 through 100 with default 20; reject invalid limit and invalid cursor with status 400 and {"error":"..."}. Return {"items":[...],"next_cursor":<string or null>}, with null on the last page. Update the README, run python3 -m unittest, and commit the change locally. Include appropriate tests for page boundaries, ordering, defaults and malformed inputs.

After implementation, pagination tests and malformed-input tests pass.

pr.body: `api.py` validates limits, encodes and checks cursors, and returns `items` plus `next_cursor`. `test_api.py` covers default and boundary limits, ordered multi-page traversal, invalid inputs, and oversized numeric inputs. README documents the response and errors. Assumption: cursor tokens encode the last item ID and are accepted only when they identify an item in the in-memory catalogue. `python3 -m unittest` passed (6 tests); `git diff --check` passed.
pr.summary: Added bounded cursor pagination for the items endpoint. Before: all 57 items returned in one response. Now: callers receive ordered pages of up to 100 items and can continue with an opaque cursor.
